sections.heading: B — Audience and scope
sections.markdown:
## B — Audience and scope

Audience: first-time Hawaii class three applicants, including minors on the graduated path, learning the three categories of traffic control devices and the meaning of yellow and white centerlines, lane lines, edge lines, stop and crosswalk lines, two-way left turn lanes, obstruction, directional and railroad markings, and traffic islands in plain English.

Prerequisites: the passing and keeping-right rules of the traffic laws section, which the yellow line rules put into paint.

Scope note: the three categories of traffic control devices and every pavement marking in the chapter, centerlines, lane lines, red markings, edge lines, stop and crosswalk lines, the two-way left turn lane, obstruction, directional and railroad markings, and traffic and safety islands. Traffic signals follow in the next section.

Recall emphasis: line meanings are practiced as recall items, and marking identification feeds the dedicated recognition surface declared in part C.

corpus_stability.reason: The Hawaii Driver's Manual is a periodically reprinted reference (imprint HMG 5/2023, copyright line through 2023); the the three categories of traffic control devices and the meaning of yellow and white centerlines, lane lines, edge lines, stop and crosswalk lines, two-way left turn lanes, obstruction, directional and railroad markings, and traffic islands rules on pages 33–38 are statutory and procedural content that changes less than once a year, so no BlockedProbe.
